boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Macalester College
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe food stops with directly verified late availability, from campus service through late Saint Paul options.

cards.title: The Grille
cards.subtitle: Ruth Stricker Dayton Campus Center, Macalester College
cards.notes: Use the Campus Center option when you need food without leaving campus; check the dining page for holiday and break exceptions before heading over.
cards.short_summary: On-campus food service with a 10 p.m. closing time.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester lists The Grille in the Campus Center as open until 10:00 p.m. daily during its weekly schedule.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: 7:30 a.m.–10:00 p.m. Monday–Friday and 1:00–10:00 p.m. Saturday–Sunday; holiday hours may differ.

cards.title: Pizza Lucé St. Paul
cards.subtitle: 1183 Selby Avenue, Saint Paul
cards.notes: Plan a Selby Avenue pickup or sit-down meal; the location page lists both dine-in and delivery/curbside availability through 1 a.m.
cards.short_summary: A Selby Avenue restaurant listed open until 1 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Lucé’s St. Paul location page lists dine-in and delivery/curbside hours until 1:00 a.m. every day.
cards.access_notes: Official listing shows dine-in and delivery/curbside from 11:00 a.m.–1:00 a.m. Monday–Friday and 10:00 a.m.–1:00 a.m. Saturday–Sunday.

cards.title: Mickey’s Diner By Willy
cards.subtitle: 1950 Seventh Street West, Saint Paul
cards.notes: Keep this West Seventh diner in reserve for a meal at an unusual hour; confirm any holiday or operational changes directly before traveling.
cards.short_summary: A Saint Paul diner whose official site states 24-hour, year-round service.
cards.evidence_claim: Mickey’s Diner By Willy states on its official website that it operates 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
cards.access_notes: Official site states: “24 Hours a day . . . 365 Days a Year.”

cards.title: Taco Bell — 565 N Snelling
cards.subtitle: 565 N Snelling, Saint Paul
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru after the dining room closes; the official location page separates late drive-thru hours from earlier dine-in availability.
cards.short_summary: A Snelling Avenue drive-thru listed as late as 4 a.m. on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-thru service at 565 N Snelling until 3:00 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 4:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru: 6:00 a.m.–3:00 a.m. Sunday–Thursday; 6:00 a.m.–4:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday. Dine-in hours end earlier.

cards.title: Taco Bell — 1672 Rice Street
cards.subtitle: 1672 Rice Street, Saint Paul
cards.notes: Consider this Rice Street location for a late drive-thru order; verify the location page on the day, as posted hours can change.
cards.short_summary: A Saint Paul Taco Bell listed open until 4 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell’s Saint Paul location directory lists the 1672 Rice Street restaurant as open until 4:00 a.m.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell Restaurants in Saint Paul, Minnesota
cards.access_notes: The official city directory lists 1672 Rice Street as “Open til 4:00AM” and identifies it as offering drive-thru service.

cards.title: Taco Bell — 1630 Robert Street South
cards.subtitle: 1630 Robert Street South, Saint Paul
cards.notes: Use this South Saint Paul drive-thru option for a later order, rather than relying on the earlier posted dine-in closing time.
cards.short_summary: A Robert Street drive-thru listed through 3 a.m. on later-week nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists the 1630 Robert Street South drive-thru until 2:00 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 3:00 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru hours run to 2:00 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 3:00 a.m. Thursday–Saturday; dine-in ends earlier.

cards.title: Taco Bell — 1940 Suburban Avenue
cards.subtitle: 1940 Suburban Avenue, Saint Paul
cards.notes: For the east-side route, use the late drive-thru schedule and check it before leaving; the dining room has separate earlier hours.
cards.short_summary: An east Saint Paul drive-thru listed until 2 a.m. on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists the 1940 Suburban Avenue drive-thru until 1:00 a.m. most days and 2:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru: 7:00 a.m.–1:00 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 7:00 a.m.–2:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday; dine-in ends earlier.

cards.title: Wendy’s — 1770 University Avenue West
cards.subtitle: 1770 University Avenue West, Saint Paul
cards.notes: Use the Midway location for a late food run; its official page lists the same closing time for restaurant and drive-thru service.
cards.short_summary: A University Avenue restaurant listed open until 2 a.m. daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy’s lists restaurant and drive-thru hours of 6:30 a.m.–2:00 a.m. every day at 1770 University Avenue West.
cards.access_notes: Official location hours list both restaurant and drive-thru service from 6:30 a.m. to 2:00 a.m. daily.

cards.title: Wendy’s — 612 West University Avenue
cards.subtitle: 612 West University Avenue, Saint Paul
cards.notes: Use this University Avenue location when an all-hours option fits the route; confirm service details with the restaurant before traveling overnight.
cards.short_summary: A Saint Paul Wendy’s listed open 24 hours every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy’s lists restaurant and drive-thru hours as open 24 hours every day at 612 West University Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists both restaurant and drive-thru as open 24 hours Monday through Sunday.

cards.title: Wendy’s — 255 East Maryland Avenue
cards.subtitle: 255 East Maryland Avenue, Saint Paul
cards.notes: Keep this Maryland Avenue location as another all-hours food option; use the official page to reconfirm access before making a late trip.
cards.short_summary: A Saint Paul Wendy’s listed open 24 hours every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy’s lists restaurant and drive-thru hours as open 24 hours every day at 255 East Maryland Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists both restaurant and drive-thru as open 24 hours Monday through Sunday.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Macalester spaces for studying, gathering, creating, performing, reflecting, and spending time outside class.

cards.title: Ruth Stricker Dayton Campus Center
cards.subtitle: Student-life hub
cards.notes: Use the CC as a central meeting point between classes; check its building-hours page and reserve a room ahead when planning a group gathering.
cards.short_summary: A student-centered campus hub with dining, lounges, rooms, and services.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester describes the Campus Center as a student-centered space and campus community hub with reservable spaces.
cards.access_notes: Academic-year building hours are listed as 7 a.m.–1 a.m. Monday–Friday and 10 a.m.–1 a.m. Saturday–Sunday; room use may require reservation.

cards.title: The Loch
cards.subtitle: Campus Center lower level
cards.notes: Bring a group for a low-key game or student event; the lower-level lounge has billiards tables and a performance-ready stage.
cards.short_summary: A lounge with billiards, dining during the academic year, and event infrastructure.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester identifies The Loch as a student lounge with two billiards tables, a raised stage, and space for events including performances and trivia.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Campus Center lower level; use follows Campus Center building access and event arrangements.

cards.title: McPherson Atrium
cards.subtitle: Campus Center second level
cards.notes: Meet classmates in the second-floor lounge before a meeting or program, and keep the space flexible for other campus users.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor student lounge designed for gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester calls McPherson Atrium a student lounge area and a prime gathering space for students.
cards.access_notes: Located on the second level of the Campus Center; building hours and any event use are governed by Campus Center policies.

cards.title: John B. Davis Lecture Hall
cards.subtitle: Campus Center lower level
cards.notes: Watch the college events calendar for a talk, screening, or performance held here; reserve it through campus processes for an approved event.
cards.short_summary: A 213-capacity venue for campus talks, films, and performances.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester lists John B. Davis Lecture Hall as an event space for keynote speakers, film screenings, and performances, with capacity for 213.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Campus Center lower level; attendance and reservations depend on the particular program.

cards.title: DeWitt Wallace Library
cards.subtitle: 110 S. Macalester Street
cards.notes: Choose an individual room for focused work or one of the larger collaborative areas for a project; follow the library’s shared-space guidelines.
cards.short_summary: The campus library combines individual study rooms with collaborative work areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The library says its spaces support studying, creating, and relaxing, from large open collaborative areas to individual study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Regular hours listed by the library are 8 a.m.–11 p.m. Monday–Thursday, with shorter Friday–Sunday hours; holiday and break hours vary.

cards.title: Idea Lab
cards.subtitle: DeWitt Wallace Library, second floor
cards.notes: Use the available banner paper, markers, paint, and glue to make event materials; leave enough time for a student organization’s publicity plan.
cards.short_summary: A library maker space for student-organization posters and banners.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester states that the Idea Lab on the Library’s second floor provides paper, markers, paint, glue, and other supplies for student organizations’ promotional materials.
cards.access_notes: Located on the library’s second floor; use supplies responsibly and confirm current availability with the library or student-life staff.

cards.title: Weyerhaeuser Memorial Chapel
cards.subtitle: Center for Religious and Spiritual Life
cards.notes: Step in for a quiet period of reflection or study, and check the Center for Religious and Spiritual Life schedule before joining a program.
cards.short_summary: A campus reflection space that also hosts religious and spiritual-life programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester’s admissions guide identifies the Chapel as home to the Center for Religious and Spiritual Life and describes spaces for meditation, reflection, and quiet study.
cards.source_title: 102 Things to Do at Mac | Macalester College
cards.access_notes: Check Center for Religious and Spiritual Life programming and building access before visiting; respect scheduled services and reflection use.

cards.title: The Great Lawn
cards.subtitle: Central campus green
cards.notes: On pleasant days, bring a book or meet a small group outdoors; leave room for classes, organized events, and others sharing the lawn.
cards.short_summary: A central outdoor setting used for classes, informal gatherings, and campus events.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester reports that classes form circles on the Great Lawn and documents the annual fall Involvement Fair there.
cards.source_title: Our Campus Home: A Place of Belonging, A Window to the World | Macalester College
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space with weather-dependent use; organized programs may reserve portions of the lawn.

cards.title: Shaw Field
cards.subtitle: South campus athletic green
cards.notes: Use the open field only when it is not set for athletics or a campus program; check posted event information before starting a casual game.
cards.short_summary: A named campus field that appears in Macalester’s account of informal outdoor activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester’s campus-life article specifically describes people playing spikeball on Shaw Field.
cards.source_title: Our Campus Home: A Place of Belonging, A Window to the World | Macalester College
cards.access_notes: Outdoor use is weather- and scheduling-dependent; yield to authorized athletic and campus events.

cards.entity_name: Janet Wallace Fine Arts Center Gallery
cards.title: Janet Wallace Fine Arts Center Gallery
cards.subtitle: Janet Wallace Fine Arts Center
cards.notes: Stop by to view student work, then use the comfortable seating for a short conversation or reset between classes while respecting exhibits.
cards.short_summary: A gallery with student exhibits and seating for casual gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester’s arts spaces page says the gallery provides exhibit space for student work and comfortable seating for casual gatherings.
cards.source_title: Studio and Rehearsal Spaces | Macalester College
cards.access_notes: Exhibit access and any gallery events may vary; treat displayed work and seating as shared campus resources.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-admission, no-purchase places and activities for Macalester students around Saint Paul.

cards.title: See contemporary work at Law Warschaw Gallery
cards.subtitle: Janet Wallace Fine Arts Center, Macalester College
cards.notes: Check the gallery’s current exhibition, then use the public entrance doorbell at the northeast corner of the gallery block.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery visit that is free and open to the public when programming is running.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester states that Law Warschaw Gallery programming is free and open to the public, except on Mondays when it is closed.
cards.access_notes: Closed Mondays; the official page asks off-campus visitors to use the northeast-corner doorbell.

cards.title: Claim a study-room conversation
cards.subtitle: Merriam Park Library, 1831 Marshall Avenue
cards.notes: Reserve a small study room for a focused catch-up, or ask at the desk for a walk-in room when one is available.
cards.short_summary: A free, bookable small-group space with walk-in availability when unoccupied.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Paul Public Library lists study rooms at Merriam Park as free of charge and allows walk-ins when a room is available.
cards.access_notes: Study rooms may be reserved from 24 hours to 14 days ahead; walk-ins are first-come, first-served when available.

cards.title: Wander Mia’s permanent collection
cards.subtitle: 2400 Third Avenue South, Minneapolis
cards.notes: Walk into the permanent-collection galleries together and save special exhibitions or ticketed events for another day.
cards.short_summary: General admission provides a no-ticket route through Mia’s permanent collection.
cards.evidence_claim: Mia says general admission to its permanent collection is always free and requires neither tickets nor reservations.
cards.source_title: Visit the Minneapolis Institute of Art—Always Free
cards.access_notes: Free access covers the permanent collection; special exhibitions and select events can require tickets and fees.

cards.title: Take a sculpture-garden loop
cards.subtitle: Walker Art Center campus, Minneapolis
cards.notes: Meet by Spoonbridge and Cherry, then follow the outdoor paths through the garden’s more than 60 sculptures.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor art-and-walk hang with no ticket needed.
cards.evidence_claim: Walker Art Center states that the Minneapolis Sculpture Garden is free to the public, requires no tickets, and is open daily.
cards.access_notes: Official hours are daily, 6 a.m.–midnight, year-round; check the page for closures or conditions.

cards.title: Visit Como Park Zoo
cards.subtitle: 1225 Estabrook Drive, Saint Paul
cards.notes: Use the visitor map to choose a few animal areas, and skip the optional donation kiosk if you are keeping the outing free.
cards.short_summary: A public zoo visit where admission is free and donations are optional.
cards.evidence_claim: Como states that admission to Como Park Zoo is free and visitors are welcome whether or not they make a voluntary donation.
cards.source_title: Como Park Zoo & Conservatory: Visitor Map & Hours
cards.access_notes: Hours vary seasonally: 10 a.m.–6 p.m. May 1 through Labor Day and 10 a.m.–4 p.m. otherwise.

cards.title: Warm up in the Marjorie McNeely Conservatory
cards.subtitle: Como Park Zoo & Conservatory, Saint Paul
cards.notes: Walk the conservatory displays at your own pace and treat the suggested donation as optional rather than part of admission.
cards.short_summary: A year-round indoor plant outing with voluntary, not required, donations.
cards.evidence_claim: Como states that admission to the Marjorie McNeely Conservatory is free and visitors are welcome without making a donation.
cards.source_title: Como Park Zoo & Conservatory: Visitor Map & Hours
cards.access_notes: Hours vary seasonally: 10 a.m.–6 p.m. May 1 through Labor Day and 10 a.m.–4 p.m. otherwise.

cards.title: Meet at Phalen Regional Park Beach
cards.subtitle: Phalen Regional Park, Saint Paul
cards.notes: Use the sand beach, splash pad, picnic area, or paved loop; bring what you need and avoid paid watercraft rentals.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal beach-and-park outing with free entry and parking.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Paul identifies Phalen Park Beach as a family-friendly destination with free admission and free parking.
cards.access_notes: This is seasonal; city information lists swimming-beach amenities and notes separate watercraft rentals.

cards.title: Browse the Minnesota Museum of American Art
cards.subtitle: Historic Pioneer Endicott, downtown Saint Paul
cards.notes: Plan a daytime gallery stop around the current exhibition schedule, and use the museum’s free admission instead of a ticketed event.
cards.short_summary: Downtown Saint Paul art viewing with free admission and free monthly tours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Minnesota Museum of American Art lists free admission and regular Thursday–Sunday public hours.
cards.access_notes: The official site lists Thursday–Sunday hours, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; confirm exhibition and holiday details before going.

cards.entity_name: The Smallest Museum in St. Paul
cards.title: Stop for a tiny public-art exhibit
cards.subtitle: University Avenue corridor, Saint Paul
cards.notes: Build a short walk around the current window-scale exhibit, then spend a few minutes comparing what each person notices first.
cards.short_summary: An all-year, no-admission public-art stop designed for brief visits.
cards.evidence_claim: The Smallest Museum in St. Paul says there is no admission fee, anyone can visit, and it is open year-round.
cards.source_title: About the Smallest Museum in St. Paul
cards.access_notes: The museum describes itself as open year-round; its exhibits are on the University Avenue corridor.

cards.title: Use Free Thursday Night at the History Center
cards.subtitle: Minnesota History Center, 345 West Kellogg Boulevard
cards.notes: Go Thursday between 4 and 8 p.m. for the recurring free-admission window, then explore exhibits without buying a general ticket.
cards.short_summary: A weekly evening option that includes both museum admission and parking at no charge.
cards.evidence_claim: Minnesota Historical Society states that Thursday-night visits from 4–8 p.m. receive free admission and parking at the Minnesota History Center.
cards.access_notes: Free Thursday Night runs 4–8 p.m.; verify the current Thursday schedule and any special closures before travel.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct study environments in and around DeWitt Wallace Library, with official access and room information.

cards.entity_name: DeWitt Wallace Library Level 1 Fireplace Area
cards.title: Level 1 Fireplace Area
cards.subtitle: DeWitt Wallace Library, Level 1
cards.notes: Set up near the fireplace when you want a reading break close to printing, textbook borrowing, and library help.
cards.short_summary: A ground-level library setting with a fireplace and nearby academic services.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester lists a fireplace, printing, textbook borrowing, and study activities among Level 1 offerings.
cards.access_notes: The library says current Macalester students, staff, and faculty have full access to its offerings.

cards.title: Idea Lab
cards.subtitle: DeWitt Wallace Library, Level 2
cards.notes: Bring a collaborative project here for makerspace tools, shared tables, and a workspace designed for experimenting.
cards.short_summary: A Level 2 collaborative workspace for making, testing, and group work.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester describes the Idea Lab as a collaborative workspace in DeWitt Wallace Library for students, faculty, and community.
cards.access_notes: Located on Library Level 2; classes or groups can reserve the Idea Lab through the EMS reservation system.

cards.title: Wood Room
cards.subtitle: DeWitt Wallace Library, Level 2
cards.notes: Use this named Level 2 room for a change of scene while reading for fun or working through independent coursework.
cards.short_summary: A named room on Level 2 among the library's collaborative and collection spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Level 2 floor map labels the Wood Room, and the library spaces page identifies it as a place to read for fun.
cards.source_title: DeWitt Wallace Library Level 2 Floor Map
cards.access_notes: The Wood Room is on Library Level 2; library access is stated for current Macalester students, staff, and faculty.

cards.title: Group Study Room 261
cards.subtitle: DeWitt Wallace Library, Level 2
cards.notes: Reserve this numbered Level 2 room through EMS when your group needs a defined place to work through shared material.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed Level 2 room intended for group study.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester's official Level 2 floor map identifies Room 261 as a Group Study Room.
cards.source_title: DeWitt Wallace Library Level 2 Floor Map
cards.access_notes: Level 2 group meeting rooms are reserved through EMS; individual students may reserve library study rooms.

cards.title: Group Study Room 262
cards.subtitle: DeWitt Wallace Library, Level 2
cards.notes: Book this numbered room through EMS for a group review session, planning meeting, or collaborative assignment.
cards.short_summary: A separate, map-listed Level 2 group-study room.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester's official Level 2 floor map identifies Room 262 as a Group Study Room.
cards.source_title: DeWitt Wallace Library Level 2 Floor Map
cards.access_notes: Level 2 group meeting rooms are reserved through EMS; individual students may reserve library study rooms.

cards.title: Group Study Room 263
cards.subtitle: DeWitt Wallace Library, Level 2
cards.notes: Use EMS to reserve this designated room when your work benefits from gathering a project team in one place.
cards.short_summary: A distinct, official-map group-study room on the library's second level.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester's official Level 2 floor map identifies Room 263 as a Group Study Room.
cards.source_title: DeWitt Wallace Library Level 2 Floor Map
cards.access_notes: Level 2 group meeting rooms are reserved through EMS; individual students may reserve library study rooms.

cards.title: Group Study Room 264
cards.subtitle: DeWitt Wallace Library, Level 2
cards.notes: Reserve this map-listed room when you need a dedicated setting to compare notes, rehearse, or complete shared work.
cards.short_summary: A fourth distinct Level 2 room designated for group study.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester's official Level 2 floor map identifies Room 264 as a Group Study Room.
cards.source_title: DeWitt Wallace Library Level 2 Floor Map
cards.access_notes: Level 2 group meeting rooms are reserved through EMS; individual students may reserve library study rooms.

cards.entity_name: DeWitt Wallace Library Level 3 Individual Study Rooms
cards.title: Level 3 Individual Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: DeWitt Wallace Library, Level 3
cards.notes: Choose one of these private rooms for solo reading or focused work; they are not reservable and have no built-in tech.
cards.short_summary: Twelve individual rooms for private, technology-light study.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester states that Level 3 has 12 individual study rooms that are not reservable and have no built-in technology.
cards.access_notes: Not reservable; no built-in tech. The library grants current Macalester students, staff, and faculty full access to its offerings.

cards.entity_name: DeWitt Wallace Library Level 4 Quiet Study Spaces
cards.title: Level 4 Quiet Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: DeWitt Wallace Library, Level 4
cards.notes: Head to Level 4 for a quiet environment, then use its browsable collection to pull supporting material for your work.
cards.short_summary: A quieter upper-level library environment with nearby browsable books.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester lists a variety of quiet study spaces and a large browsable collection on Library Level 4.
cards.access_notes: The library says current Macalester students, staff, and faculty have full access to its offerings.

cards.entity_name: DeWitt Wallace Library Level 4 Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Level 4 Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: DeWitt Wallace Library, Level 4
cards.notes: Reserve a Level 4 group room through EMS when a quiet floor and a book collection suit your team's work session.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group rooms on the library's quiet fourth level.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester lists reservable group study rooms on Level 4 of DeWitt Wallace Library.
cards.access_notes: Reserve Level 4 group study rooms through EMS; library offerings have full access for current Macalester students, staff, and faculty.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on or beside the Grand Avenue corridor at Macalester College.

cards.title: French Meadow Cafe
cards.subtitle: Grand Avenue corridor, Macalester Street corner
cards.notes: Use the shared lot off Macalester Street or approach on foot from campus, then check the current menu before choosing a meal or bakery item.
cards.short_summary: A café and bakery beside Macalester Street.
cards.evidence_claim: French Meadow lists its Saint Paul café at 1662 Grand Avenue and notes parking off Macalester Street.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant service; purchase required.

cards.title: Shish A Mediterranean Grill & Cafe
cards.subtitle: Grand Avenue corridor, near Macalester Street
cards.notes: Add this Mediterranean grill to a Grand Avenue walk and consult its current menu or ordering information before arranging a meal.
cards.short_summary: A Mediterranean food stop one block from campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Saint Paul lists Shish A Mediterranean Grill & Cafe at 1668 Grand Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant service; purchase required.

cards.title: Italian Pie Shoppe
cards.subtitle: Grand Avenue corridor, near Macalester Street
cards.notes: Use this Grand Avenue pizza destination for a sit-down or takeout meal; review the restaurant’s current service details before going.
cards.short_summary: A pizza-focused stop beside the campus blocks.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Saint Paul lists Italian Pie Shoppe at 1670 Grand Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant service; purchase required.

cards.title: Sencha Tea Bar
cards.subtitle: Grand Avenue corridor, west of Macalester Street
cards.notes: Pause for loose-leaf tea, a tea latte, or bubble tea, and use the shop’s current menu to plan an order before walking over.
cards.short_summary: A tea-bar stop on the campus-side corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Saint Paul lists Sencha Tea Bar at 1692 Grand Avenue, and Sencha says its tea bars serve bubble tea, tea lattes, and brewed loose-leaf tea.
cards.access_notes: Retail beverage service; purchase required.

cards.title: Catzen Coffee
cards.subtitle: Grand Avenue corridor, east of Snelling Avenue
cards.notes: Reserve lounge time if you want to visit the resident cats; the coffee-shop seating is a separate option for drinks, snacks, books, or games.
cards.short_summary: Coffee shop and reservable cat lounge.
cards.evidence_claim: Catzen Coffee lists its location at 1416 Grand Avenue and says its Cat Lounge uses reservations.
cards.access_notes: Cat Lounge reservations are required; a coffee-shop purchase is required for lounge entry for groups of one to four.

cards.title: Dunn Bros Coffee
cards.subtitle: Grand Avenue corridor, Snelling Avenue corner
cards.notes: Use this corner coffee shop as a simple meet-up point just east of campus, then order a drink or food item if you decide to stay.
cards.short_summary: Coffee stop at the Grand and Snelling corner.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Saint Paul identifies Dunn Bros Coffee at 1569 Grand Avenue, on the corner of Grand and Snelling avenues.
cards.access_notes: Retail café; purchase required.

cards.title: St. Paul Cheese Shop
cards.subtitle: Grand Avenue corridor, by Snelling Avenue
cards.notes: Browse the cheese counter or arrange a sandwich stop while walking the Grand Avenue commercial strip just east of Macalester’s main intersection.
cards.short_summary: Cheese counter and food stop near Snelling.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Saint Paul lists St. Paul Cheese Shop at 1573 Grand Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Retail food shop; purchase required.

cards.title: Breadsmith
cards.subtitle: Grand Avenue corridor, by Snelling Avenue
cards.notes: Pick up a loaf, pastry, or other baked item from this bakery on the eastbound Grand Avenue route from Macalester’s Snelling Avenue corner.
cards.short_summary: An artisan bakery immediately east of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Breadsmith’s Twin Cities ordering page lists its St. Paul location at 1579 Grand Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Retail bakery; purchase required.

cards.title: Whole Foods Market St. Paul
cards.subtitle: Grand Avenue corridor, at Fairview Avenue
cards.notes: Walk or take transit west along Grand to Fairview for groceries and prepared-food options; check the store page for current departments and services.
cards.short_summary: A full grocery stop beside the west Grand corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Whole Foods Market lists its St. Paul store at 30 South Fairview Avenue, adjacent to Grand Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Retail grocery store; purchases required for merchandise.

cards.title: Bruegger's Bagels
cards.subtitle: Grand Avenue corridor, east toward Lexington Parkway
cards.notes: Use this bakery-café as a breakfast or lunch stop farther east on Grand; check its location page for current daily service information first.
cards.short_summary: A bagel and coffee stop on east Grand.
cards.evidence_claim: Bruegger’s lists its Grand Avenue location at 800 Grand Avenue in Saint Paul.
cards.access_notes: Retail restaurant; purchase required.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Macalester rituals and recurring campus events, from a paintable boulder to snow-day Pushball.

cards.title: Paint The Rock
cards.subtitle: A 700-pound campus boulder
cards.notes: Bring an approved message and supplies, then add a fresh layer to this long-running campus rite of passage. Ask campus staff about current painting guidance.
cards.short_summary: Macalester’s paintable 700-pound boulder turns student messages into a changing public landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester identifies painting The Rock as a campus rite of passage and describes it as a 700-pound boulder.
cards.access_notes: Follow current campus guidance before painting.

cards.title: Pushball in the Snow
cards.subtitle: A giant-ball campus game
cards.notes: Watch the Program Board calendar for the next installment, then join the group effort to move the oversized inflatable ball across a snowy field.
cards.short_summary: Pushball converts a snowy lawn and an oversized inflatable ball into a Macalester group game.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester describes Pushball as a recently revived tradition using an approximately eight-foot inflatable ball in freshly fallen snow.
cards.access_notes: Check Program Board announcements for scheduling and participation details.

cards.title: Winter Ball
cards.subtitle: Program Board’s winter tradition
cards.notes: Look for the Program Board’s event details during the academic year and follow its venue, ticketing, attire, and entry instructions for that edition.
cards.short_summary: Winter Ball is one of the recurring traditions organized by Macalester’s student Program Board.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester’s Center for Student Leadership and Engagement lists Winter Ball among Program Board’s well-beloved traditions.
cards.access_notes: Format, access, and any cost vary by year; consult the current event listing.

cards.title: Celebrate Founding Day
cards.subtitle: Macalester’s birthday observance
cards.notes: Follow the college’s Founding Day announcements to see that year’s birthday events and historical programming; the tradition was revived in 2004.
cards.short_summary: Founding Day marks Macalester’s 1874 charter and has returned as a recurring college birthday celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester says Founding Day began in 1938, commemorates its March 5, 1874 charter, and was revived in March 2004.
cards.access_notes: Programming changes by year; use the college’s current Founding Day information.

cards.title: Bingo for Books
cards.subtitle: An early-year Program Board event
cards.notes: Check Program Board announcements near the start of the academic year, arrive according to the event instructions, and play the campus version of bingo.
cards.short_summary: Bingo for Books is Macalester’s recurring early-year bingo tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester describes Bingo for Books as an annual beginning-of-year tradition, and its student leadership office lists it among Program Board traditions.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current date, venue, entry process, and any cost with Program Board.

cards.title: Springfest
cards.subtitle: A Program Board spring tradition
cards.notes: Monitor the Program Board calendar in spring for the lineup and location, then take in the event’s music and outdoor campus atmosphere.
cards.short_summary: Springfest is a recurring Macalester spring event associated with local bands and campus downtime.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester’s student leadership office lists Springfest among Program Board’s well-beloved traditions; an admissions page describes it as an April event with local bands.
cards.access_notes: Check the current Program Board listing for access and schedule details.

cards.title: Midnight Breakfast
cards.subtitle: A fall-semester study-break tradition
cards.notes: Watch for the end-of-semester announcement and follow the dining event’s entry details; it pairs nighttime breakfast with a pause before study days.
cards.short_summary: Midnight Breakfast is Macalester’s fall-semester nighttime breakfast study break.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester calls Midnight Breakfast a tradition held at the end of the fall semester, and an alumni story documents its annual Mock Weekly distribution.
cards.access_notes: Attendance and dining access may be limited to the campus community; verify the current event notice.

cards.title: Hear the Peace Prayer
cards.subtitle: An opening-and-closing academic-year reading
cards.notes: Attend Opening Convocation, major gatherings, or Commencement when open to observe students read the prayer in their native languages.
cards.short_summary: The Peace Prayer bookends Macalester’s academic year through multilingual student readings.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester states that five students read the Peace Prayer in their native tongues at Opening Convocation, major gatherings, and Commencement.
cards.access_notes: Public access depends on the particular college ceremony.

cards.entity_name: Minnesota Scottish Fair and Highland Games
cards.title: Scottish Fair at Macalester
cards.subtitle: A recurring campus-hosted Highland gathering
cards.notes: Use the Pipe Band’s current announcement and the fair organizer’s event information before visiting; campus hosting is scheduled for July 18, 2026.
cards.short_summary: Macalester’s Pipe Band continues a campus connection to the Minnesota Scottish Fair and Highland Games.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester says the fair first came to campus in 1973 and its Pipe Band page announces the 2026 fair on the Macalester campus.
cards.access_notes: The 2026 Pipe Band announcement directs visitors to the fair organizer for current event details.

cards.title: Pick Up The MOCK Weekly
cards.subtitle: The Mac Weekly’s Midnight Breakfast edition
cards.notes: At fall-semester Midnight Breakfast, look for The Mac Weekly’s humorous special issue, created by the staff for distribution before campus study days.
cards.short_summary: The MOCK Weekly is a recurring satirical special edition timed to Midnight Breakfast.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester’s alumni publication states that The Mac Weekly staff creates the humorous MOCK Weekly each fall semester to distribute at Midnight Breakfast.
cards.source_title: My Time as an Editor for The Mac Weekly
cards.access_notes: Availability is tied to the fall Midnight Breakfast event and may be limited.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Macalester College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key first-weekend sequence that starts on campus, makes room for student-life discovery, and ends with familiar places to return to during the term.

cards.title: Begin with the chapel
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · campus orientation stop
cards.notes: Walk through the chapel during its posted open hours, locate the lower-level resources, and save it as a quiet landmark for future campus meetups.
cards.short_summary: An opening stop that pairs campus orientation with a recognizable gathering place.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester states that Weyerhaeuser Memorial Chapel hosts worship, lectures, art, music events, and other community functions, and publishes its open hours.
cards.source_title: Our Spaces | Center for Religious and Spiritual Life
cards.access_notes: The college lists chapel hours as Monday–Thursday 8:30 a.m.–9:30 p.m. and Friday 8:30 a.m.–8 p.m.; confirm any event-specific access.

cards.title: Get your bearings on the Great Lawn
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · central campus
cards.notes: Use this open landmark to orient yourself between nearby buildings, then take a short daylight loop to identify routes you will use during the week.
cards.short_summary: A central outdoor pause for learning the campus layout.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester identifies the Great Lawn on its campus map and describes it as a campus gathering space in its campus coverage.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access depends on weather and campus conditions; stay on public campus paths and follow posted event guidance.

cards.title: Make your first dinner simple
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Ruth Stricker Dayton Campus Center
cards.notes: Check the current dining page before you go, then use dinner to compare meal-plan logistics and arrange a low-pressure plan with new neighbors.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus dinner stop with published meal-plan and service details.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester's 2026–27 dining information lists Café Mac in the Campus Center, accepted payment methods, and meal service periods.
cards.access_notes: Café Mac accepts meal swipes, Flex points, Mac Money, and credit cards; verify holiday and break hours on the dining site.

cards.title: Save a few groups to explore
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · student-life planning stop
cards.notes: Browse the active organizations directory, save a handful that genuinely interest you, and check each listing later for meeting details or upcoming events.
cards.short_summary: A practical way to turn broad interests into specific campus connections.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester directs students to Highland Hub to browse active student organizations, meeting times, and organization events.
cards.access_notes: Organization participation and meeting schedules vary; use Highland Hub or the organization directly for current information.

cards.title: Choose one current campus program
cards.subtitle: Friday night · flexible campus event slot
cards.notes: Filter the calendar for an event you can attend this weekend, then confirm its location, start time, admission details, and any registration instructions.
cards.short_summary: A flexible evening choice grounded in the live campus calendar.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester's official events calendar includes filters for campus events, arts, athletics, films, lectures, and student-organization events.
cards.source_title: Event Search | Macalester College Events Calendar
cards.access_notes: Admission, audience eligibility, and scheduling vary by listing; check the individual event page before attending.

cards.title: Take an active Saturday break
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · campus athletics facility
cards.notes: Check the space schedule, then choose an available activity such as swimming, fitness, or open recreation rather than arriving with a fixed plan.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation stop with several possible activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester identifies the Leonard Center as its athletics facility and states that students can swim, run, lift weights, and play ping pong there.
cards.source_title: Classes and Programs | Wellness and Health at Macalester
cards.access_notes: Space schedules and reservations can change; the athletics department directs users to the EMS schedule for current availability.

cards.title: Look in on the current gallery show
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Janet Wallace Fine Arts Commons
cards.notes: Check what is currently installed, take time with one or two works, and look for related public talks or presentations before you leave campus.
cards.short_summary: A compact art stop inside Macalester's Fine Arts Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester states that the Law Warschaw Gallery is in the Janet Wallace Fine Arts Commons and hosts five to six exhibitions annually.
cards.source_title: Majors and Minors | Art and Art History
cards.access_notes: Exhibition dates and public access can vary; verify the current exhibition and building access before visiting.

cards.title: Check for a music performance
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · Music Building
cards.notes: Look at the music and events calendars for a performance, then confirm whether the particular program is open to students and whether a ticket is required.
cards.short_summary: A performance-oriented stop at Macalester's accessible recital hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Macalester describes Mairs Concert Hall as a 317-seat, fully accessible recital hall used for Music Department concerts, student recitals, and guest performances.
cards.access_notes: This is a performance venue, not general drop-in space; confirm the current program's time, audience rules, and ticketing.

cards.title: Spend Sunday outside at Como
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · Saint Paul
cards.notes: Choose a daylight route on the paved trails, bring water, and use the city page to plan around the park's many facilities without trying to fit them all in.
cards.short_summary: A nearby city-park outing built around a short outdoor reset.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Saint Paul lists Como Regional Park's 2.3 miles of paved trails and its broad set of park facilities.
cards.source_title: Como Regional Park | City of Saint Paul
cards.access_notes: The City lists park hours from sunrise to 11 p.m.; use daylight for the walk and check separate attraction pages for facility-specific access.

cards.title: End with a library reset
cards.subtitle: Sunday evening · 110 South Macalester Street
cards.notes: Find a study floor, browse the research guides, and identify the service desk so the building feels familiar before your first week becomes busy.
cards.short_summary: A quiet final stop that establishes a useful academic routine.
cards.evidence_claim: DeWitt Wallace Library provides research guides and study spaces, and publishes regular Sunday hours of 10 a.m.–11 p.m.
cards.access_notes: The library lists regular Sunday hours of 10 a.m.–11 p.m.; breaks and holidays can change access, so verify before a late visit.

warnings: Event availability, venue access, and campus schedules can change; verify the direct source before attending.
